page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Feedback inhibition defined
steps.margin_note: Three lines. The phrase 'end product' has to appear.
lines: Feedback inhibition is a cellular control
mechanism in which an enzyme's activity is
inhibited by the enzyme's own END PRODUCT.
steps.why: The product of the pathway is also the signal that stops it, which is what makes the control a feedback rather than an ordinary inhibition.
common_mistakes: Saying the substrate inhibits the enzyme. It is the END PRODUCT.
Calling it competitive inhibition. Feedback inhibition is its own named type.
steps.memory_tip: The product feeds back and shuts the tap.

steps.label: Why the cell does it
steps.margin_note: Name it as homeostatic control and say what is saved.

The cell stops making a product once it has
enough, so raw material and energy are not
steps.why: Without feedback, a pathway would keep running while its product piled up, which would waste both the starting material and the ATP spent on the pathway.
common_mistakes: Giving no purpose. The reason the cell does it is the second mark.
Saying it speeds the reaction up. It SLOWS or stops the reaction.
steps.memory_tip: Stop when you have enough, and nothing is wasted.
